title: Rigveda 9.25: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.25: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.25 is a hymn of 6 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 677v-678r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.25.1-5 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 15); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 677v
translation.original_text:
1pava̍sva dakṣa̱sādha̍no de̱vebhya̍ḥ pī̱taye̍ hare | ma̱rudbhyo̍ vā̱yave̱ mada̍ḥ ||
2pava̍māna dhi̱yā hi̱to̱3̱̍ 'bhi yoni̱ṁ kani̍kradat | dharma̍ṇā vā̱yum ā vi̍śa ||
3saṁ de̱vaiḥ śo̍bhate̱ vṛṣā̍ ka̱vir yonā̱v adhi̍ pri̱yaḥ | vṛ̱tra̱hā de̍va̱vīta̍maḥ ||
4viśvā̍ rū̱pāṇy ā̍vi̱śan pu̍nā̱no yā̍ti harya̱taḥ | yatrā̱mṛtā̍sa̱ āsa̍te ||
5a̱ru̱ṣo ja̱naya̱n gira̱ḥ soma̍ḥ pavata āyu̱ṣak | indra̱ṁ gaccha̍n ka̱vikra̍tuḥ ||
translation.text:
1GREEN-HUED! as one who giveth strength flow on for Gods to drink, a draught For Vâyu and the Marut host.
2O Pavamâna, sent by song, roaring about thy dwelling-place, Pass into Vâyu as Law bids.
3The Steer shines with the Deities, dear Sage in his appointed home, Foe-Slayer, most beloved by Gods.
4Taking each beauteous form, he goes, desirable, while purified, Thither where- the Immortals sit.
5To Indra Soma flows, the Red, engendering song, exceeding wise, The visitor of living men.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 677v (numbered 99v by the scribe) (OPenn image 678, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.24.3 ‹nṛ-bhiḥ yataḥ vi nīyase›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 678r (numbered 100r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.25.6 ‹-yonim āsadam›. Verses 9.25.1-5 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1pavasva | dakṣa-sādhanaḥ | devebhyaḥ | pītaye | hare | marut-bhyaḥ | vāyave | madaḥ
2pavamāna | dhiyā | hitaḥ | abhi | yonim | kanikradat | dharmaṇā | vāyum | ā | viśa
3sam | devaiḥ | śobhate | vṛṣā | kaviḥ | yonau | adhi | priyaḥ | vṛtra-hā | deva-vītamaḥ
4viśvā | rūpāṇi | ā-viśan | punānaḥ | yāti | haryataḥ | yatra | amṛtāsaḥ | āsate
5aruṣaḥ | janayan | giraḥ | somaḥ | pavate | āyuṣak | indram | gacchan | kavi-kratuḥ

translation.original_ref: RV 9.25.6 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 15); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 678r
translation.original_text: <sup>6</sup>ā pa̍vasva madintama pa̱vitra̱ṁ dhāra̍yā kave | a̱rkasya̱ yoni̍m ā̱sada̍m ||
translation.text: <sup>6</sup>Flow, best exhilarator, Sage, flow to the filter in a stream To seat thee in the place of song.
